sentences.show: Napoleon marched into Russia with more than 450,000 men. He left it on a sled.
On this day in 1812, his retreating army was beaten at Vyazma.
He had taken Moscow in September, and found it empty, and on fire.
Now, with no peace and no supplies, the Grand Army turned for home.
Then came the snow, and the frost.
There was no winter clothing, no food, no fodder for the horses. Cossacks attacked the columns day and night.
When a horse fell, starving soldiers cut it up before it had even died.
At the Berezina river, full of drifting ice, the army was trapped.
It was saved by a general who had disobeyed Napoleon, and kept his bridge-building tools.
By then, only about 49,000 fighting men were left.
In December, Napoleon left his army behind, and rode for Paris in a sled.
Also on this day: the dog Laika went into orbit, and the writer Olympe de Gouges went to the guillotine.
